title: Knock
summary: "Knock" is a short science fiction story by Fredric Brown, first published in the mid-twentieth century and widely anthologized. It opens with a famous two-sentence horror setup, "The last man on Earth sat alone in a room. There was a knock on the door...", and then subverts the expected dread. The narrator, Walter Phelan, a mild-mannered anthropology professor, is one of the few human survivors of an alien invasion. The Zan, a race of tall, emotionless beings who look nothing like humans, have wiped out Earth's population with a vibration weapon and kept a zoo of specimens aboard their ship. Walter, who has been placed in a cubicle with a woman named Grace Evans, works with the aliens to understand their immortality and their mistaken assumptions about mortal creatures. The tale is a witty, ironic piece of wry humour in which the knock at the door turns out to be harmless, and the story ends on a playful note about the future of the human race. Brown's story is known for its brevity, its dry comedy, and its inversion of the expected menace.
